senses.gloss: f. (ballistra, βάλιστρα) catapult, a war engine for throwing stones, or (b. manualis) for arrows.
units: <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2:4">Lam. R. to II, 2</cite> <he>אבני ב׳</he> stones thrown from the catapult.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 8:3:2">Y. Sot. VIII, 22ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>ברד כנגד בליצטורא שלהן</he>; (Mekh. Bshall. s. 2 <he>בלסטראות</he>, pl.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 232:2">Yalk. Ex. 232</cite> <he>בלסיטראות</he>, read <he>בליסט׳</he>) the hail stones correspond to the catapults in the warfare of men.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 17:1">Pesik. R. s. 17</cite>; Pesik. Vayhi p. 67ᵃ <he>אבני בלסתרא</he> (corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 29:1">Pesik. R. s. 29—30</cite> (p. 139ᵇ ed. Fr.) <he>את האבן בליסטרה</he> (read <he>אבן הבל׳</he>). Lam. R. introd. (R. Josh. 2) <he>אבני בליסטרוס</he> (read … <he>רא</he>); a. fr.—Pl. <he>בַּלִּיסְטְרָאוֹת</he>. Yalk. l. c., v. supra. Tanḥ. Bo 4; Shof’tim 14. Mekh. l. c.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 18:12">Midr. Till. to Ps. XVIII</cite>.
